squawks.headline: China's central bank governor Pan calls for cooperation with the EU as officials discuss exchange rates
squawks.detail: Chinese and EU officials discussed exchange rates on Monday, and PBOC Governor Pan called for dialogue and cooperation with the bloc, Reuters reports. European officials had raised their concerns about the yuan's value and China's trade surplus with the EU.

squawks.headline: US 3-month and 6-month bill auctions clear at higher yields of 4.18% and 4.34%, with weaker cover
squawks.detail: The US Treasury's 3-month bill sold at a high yield of 4.18%, up from 4.155%, with bid-to-cover of 2.74 against 2.76 previously. The 6-month bill sold at 4.34%, up from 4.31%, with bid-to-cover of 2.6 against 2.83 previously.

squawks.headline: Russia says it will not agree to a new grain deal
squawks.detail: Russia's permanent mission to the UN said Moscow will not sign up to a new grain deal, according to the TASS news agency.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says he is not currently proposing a rerun of the EU referendum
squawks.detail: The Prime Minister made the remark on Monday as he set out the UK-EU summit deal to parliament.

squawks.headline: Sterling edges up against the dollar but gives back some earlier gains as the dollar steadies
squawks.detail: Reuters reports the pound edged higher against the dollar on Monday, paring some earlier gains as the dollar steadied and investors assessed new signals on the economic outlook. No levels were given.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says the UK could not rejoin the EU without a referendum
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said on Monday that taking the UK back into the EU without a referendum would be unthinkable. He spoke as the government presses ahead with its EU summit deal.

squawks.headline: US crude oil drops below $80 a barrel for the first time since August
squawks.detail: US crude futures fell under $80 per barrel on Monday afternoon, their lowest level since August, according to a market newswire report.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says the EU deal is worth up to 0.5% of the UK economy and both sides will avoid policies that hurt each other's industries
squawks.detail: UK Prime Minister Burnham put the value of the EU deal at up to 0.5% of the British economy. He also said the UK and the EU will avoid policies that harm each other's industries.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says the bill implementing the EU deal will be introduced on Thursday
squawks.detail: In remarks on the EU deal, PM Burnham said legislation to implement it will be brought forward on Thursday. He also said the UK and EU will avoid policies that harm each other's industries.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham tells parliament the EU summit deal will bring real benefits and calls for a more constructive EU relationship
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Andy Burnham made a statement to parliament following the EU-UK summit agreements. He described Friday as a landmark moment and said there is a clear consensus among Britons for closer ties with the EU.

squawks.headline: Fitch says the outlook for US banks in 2027 is deteriorating as risks rise
squawks.detail: Fitch Ratings published a weaker 2027 outlook for the US banking sector, pointing to rising risks.

squawks.headline: Libya's Tripoli government condemns Ukraine's announced operations against Russian naval vessels off Benghazi
squawks.detail: Libya's Tripoli-based Government of National Unity says it rejects any foreign military operations on its territory or in its waters, and says it has authorised none. It also warns against any use of Libyan ports and facilities for military purposes.

squawks.headline: EU's 22nd Russia sanctions package cuts 60 banks off SWIFT, adds 70 shadow fleet ships and covers electricity services
squawks.detail: European Commission President von der Leyen said the package targets financial services and crypto, removing 60 Russian banks from SWIFT and setting up a crypto sanctions task force. It also lists 70 more shadow fleet vessels, covers electricity services for the first time, bars European countries from helping Russia rebuild energy facilities and stops Europeans from holding posts in Russian companies.

squawks.headline: EU presents its 22nd package of sanctions on Russia
squawks.detail: A market news feed reports that the EU has presented its 22nd sanctions package against Russia. No details of the measures were given.

squawks.headline: ECB's Panetta warns that fragmenting payment systems risk raising costs and weakening economic ties
squawks.detail: ECB policymaker Fabio Panetta said on Monday that payment systems are becoming tools of geopolitical power, and that a push for national autonomy could fragment networks, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham to use Henry VIII powers to fast-track adoption of EU rules, Telegraph reports
squawks.detail: The Telegraph reports that the government plans to use Henry VIII clauses so the Prime Minister can amend legislation to bring in EU rules with minimal Commons scrutiny.

squawks.headline: Czech PM Babis rejects the next EU budget proposal and says positions are too far apart to see a deal
squawks.detail: Czech Prime Minister Babis called the current proposal for the next EU budget unacceptable and said he disagrees with the proposed split of funding between national and centrally run programmes. He also said financing for Ukraine should sit outside the EU budget.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says security guarantees for Ukraine should come close to NATO membership
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz said the planned security guarantees for Ukraine would come close to NATO accession. He also said it was a mistake not to admit Ukraine to NATO in 2008.

squawks.headline: NATO's Rutte says every incident in Europe will bring more support for Ukraine and NATO must not be pushed back to its 1997 borders
squawks.detail: NATO Secretary General Rutte said the alliance has response options to Russia's hybrid war that the public may not always see, and that only allies decide on NATO membership. He also said the US and Europe are aligned.

squawks.headline: US flash composite PMI falls to 54.6 from 55.9, below the 55.6 forecast, as manufacturing eases to 54.5
squawks.detail: The S&P Global flash composite PMI for the US came in at 54.6 against a forecast of 55.6 and a previous reading of 55.9. The flash manufacturing PMI was 54.5, matching the forecast and down from 54.9.

squawks.headline: Merz calls reports of a Russian nuclear-armed satellite shocking and says NATO's eastern flank needs stronger defence
squawks.detail: Germany's chancellor said the reports that Russia is ready to launch a nuclear-armed satellite were not new but still shocking. He said defence of NATO's eastern flank will be discussed this week and must be stronger than before.

squawks.headline: Macron proposes a constitutional 'golden rule' to cap French government spending and contain deficits
squawks.detail: The FT reports that the French president has suggested a constitutional reform to limit government spending and keep future deficits in check. The proposal is similar to ones put forward by his opponents.

squawks.headline: German Chancellor Merz says Europe is ready to negotiate with Russia and urges Moscow to halt provocations over Poland
squawks.detail: Merz also said NATO threatens no one, freedom of navigation must be upheld, and there is intense communication over the Baltic Sea to avoid escalation. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: BoE chief economist Pill says action is needed now to keep prices stable
squawks.detail: Bank of England chief economist and MPC member Huw Pill said policy action should be taken now to preserve price stability, according to a market news feed. No further detail on the occasion or any market reaction was given.

squawks.headline: Traders increase bets on BoE and ECB rate hikes after Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive
squawks.detail: Market reports say traders added to BoE and ECB rate-hike bets after the Nvidia news. Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang with immediate effect, and its shares rose more than 30% in pre-market trading, according to the FT.

squawks.headline: Bank of Israel leaves its interest rate unchanged, Israeli reports say
squawks.detail: Reports in Israel say the Bank of Israel has kept its policy rate unchanged. The reports did not give the rate level.

squawks.headline: Russia accuses Estonia of letting Ukraine use its airspace for attacks and warns this risks open war with Russia
squawks.detail: Russia's foreign ministry says Estonia lets Ukraine use its airspace to attack Russia and is trying to obstruct Russian cargo ships in the Baltic Sea. The ministry says such actions are close to triggering an open war with Russia.

squawks.headline: India's trade secretary says a fix on bulk Scotch tariffs is being sought quickly, as negotiators were unaware of Indian court cases
squawks.detail: India's trade secretary said negotiators on both sides of the India-UK trade agreement did not know about court cases in India on the tariff issues. He said India is working to resolve the bulk Scotch tariff dispute as quickly as it can.

squawks.headline: US Chicago Fed National Activity Index falls to -0.06 in October, missing the 0.2 forecast
squawks.detail: The Chicago Fed National Activity Index came in at -0.06 for October, below the 0.2 forecast. September's reading was revised to 0.05 from 0.07.

squawks.headline: India's trade secretary says blocked containers of bulk Scotch have been released from Indian ports
squawks.detail: India's trade secretary said shipping containers of bulk Scotch held at Indian ports have been released, and that the UK government has raised the Scotch whisky tariff issue with India. He added that he sees no problem with other countries under the trade pact after the dispute.

squawks.headline: US Treasury counsellor Zervos says financial conditions tightened last week
squawks.detail: Zervos, a counsellor at the US Treasury, said financial conditions tightened over the past week. The remarks come as a global market selloff continues.

squawks.headline: India seeks legal opinion to resolve a dispute over tariffs on bulk Scotch under the UK trade pact
squawks.detail: India's trade secretary says the trade ministry is working with the finance ministry on technical solutions to the tariff issue on bulk Scotch. He says differing court orders and legal interpretations have complicated the issue.

squawks.headline: India's trade secretary says India is sticking to its commitments under the India-UK trade agreement
squawks.detail: India's trade secretary said India continues to honour its commitments under the India-UK trade agreement. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Iran's Araghchi says the foreign ministry must pursue talks and seek to have sanctions lifted through dialogue
squawks.detail: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said his ministry is responsible for pursuing negotiations and trying to get sanctions lifted through dialogue, according to reports. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Dollar index climbs to a fresh 19-month high
squawks.detail: A market newswire reports the US dollar index has reached its highest level in 19 months. No figure for the index level was given.

squawks.headline: UK PM's spokesman says talks with the EU on options for ties are starting, with no commitment to tariffs on Chinese EVs
squawks.detail: The Prime Minister's spokesman said the UK is opening talks with the EU on realistic options for the relationship. He added that the UK has made no commitment to the EU to impose tariffs on electric vehicles from China.

squawks.headline: Allies warn Russia may launch a nuclear space weapon as soon as next month
squawks.detail: Western allies have warned that Russia may launch a nuclear-armed space weapon next month, according to a market news feed. This follows the German government saying it takes reports of such a satellite very seriously.

squawks.headline: NATO's Rutte says the US is fully aligned with Ukraine and the EU and the alliance will never start an attack
squawks.detail: NATO Secretary General Rutte said the alliance is defensive and that none of its members would start an attack on another nation. He added that the US is completely aligned with Ukraine and the EU.

squawks.headline: ONS linked employer-employee data shows about 60,000 fewer UK workers a month moving to better-paying firms than before the pandemic
squawks.detail: New ONS linked employee-employer data show 56% of job-to-job moves are to a firm that pays more on average. Around 60,000 fewer employees a month make such a switch than before the pandemic, according to an economist's reading of the release.

squawks.headline: NATO's Rutte says the alliance would defend itself if attacked, after Russian missiles entered Polish airspace
squawks.detail: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said members would have to defend themselves in the event of an attack. He spoke after earlier calling the Russian missile incursion into Poland a dangerous incident. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: NATO's Rutte calls Russian missiles entering Poland a dangerous incident and says it must be established whether it was intentional
squawks.detail: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said Russian missiles had entered Polish territory and called it a dangerous incident. He said the authorities need to establish whether it was intentional.

squawks.headline: German government condemns Russian airspace violations over Poland and calls Moscow's tougher stance on NATO unacceptable
squawks.detail: A German government spokesperson strongly condemned Russian violations of Polish airspace. The spokesperson said Russia's more aggressive posture towards NATO was unacceptable.

squawks.headline: ECB's Simkus says a December hike may not fully contain inflation but sees no urgency for a follow-up move
squawks.detail: Lithuanian ECB policymaker Gediminas Simkus said a rate rise next month may fall short of fully containing inflation, but a further move is not urgent as second-round effects are building only gradually, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: EU Council approves the EU's 2027 budget
squawks.detail: The EU Council announced it has given final approval to the bloc's budget for 2027.

squawks.headline: German government says it takes very seriously reports that Russia is ready to launch a nuclear-armed satellite
squawks.detail: A German government spokesperson responded on Monday to reports that Russia is ready to launch a nuclear-armed satellite, saying Berlin was treating them very seriously. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Hungary's PM Magyar rejects EU budget draft and says Costa's latest proposal does not bring a deal closer
squawks.detail: Hungarian Prime Minister Magyar said Hungary cannot accept the previously published EU budget version and that European Council President Costa's new proposal from Saturday does not move the sides closer to agreement. He also said the EU budget and financial support for Ukraine should be handled separately.

squawks.headline: Kremlin warns of rising terrorist activity in the Baltic Sea and says Russia will keep up daily strikes in response to Ukrainian attacks
squawks.detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said an attack on a Russian ship has raised tensions in the Baltic and called on Baltic Sea states to use their influence on Kyiv. He also said Russia's response to recent Ukrainian attacks will be continued daily strikes on Ukrainian military infrastructure, and dismissed reports that Russia is preparing a nuclear-armed satellite.

squawks.headline: Libya's Sharara oil pipeline reopens and crude pumping resumes, NOC chairman says
squawks.detail: The chairman of Libya's National Oil Corporation says the Sharara pipeline has reopened and crude is flowing again. The NOC had earlier said a pipeline valve closure would cut Sharara output by about 350,000 bpd.

squawks.headline: Haigh says UK reindustrialisation depends on lowering energy costs and pledges to stop payments for unused power
squawks.detail: First Secretary Haigh said bringing industry back to the UK requires action on energy costs. He also said consumers should no longer pay for electricity that cannot be used.

squawks.headline: Haigh calls the UK's current set-up for water and energy a global outlier and says public control need not cause alarm
squawks.detail: First Secretary Haigh said the UK's existing arrangements for water and energy are unusual by international standards and that public control should not worry anyone. She added that competition should be left alone where it already works.

squawks.headline: Russian oil exports from Baltic and Black Sea terminals face growing delays from bad weather and Ukrainian drone attacks
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that loadings at Russia's main western oil export terminals are being held up by bad weather and repeated Ukrainian drone strikes. Its sources are traders, people with direct knowledge of loading schedules, and shipping data.

squawks.headline: UK flash composite PMI falls to 52.3 from 52.9 as services slip to 52 and manufacturing to 52.7, all below forecasts
squawks.detail: The UK flash PMIs for November show the composite at 52.3 against a 52.8 forecast and 52.9 previously. Services came in at 52 (forecast 53, previous 52.8) and manufacturing at 52.7 (forecast 53, previous 52.8).

squawks.headline: Eurozone flash composite PMI holds at 51.7, below the 52 forecast, as services slip to 51.2 and manufacturing rises to 52.9
squawks.detail: The November flash composite PMI for the eurozone was unchanged at 51.7, missing the 52 forecast. Services fell to 51.2 from 51.4, below the 51.8 forecast, and manufacturing rose to 52.9 from 52.7, above the 52.7 forecast.

squawks.headline: Zelenskyy says Ukraine needs answers on Article 5-style security guarantees
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskyy said Kyiv requires clarity on Article 5 security guarantees, after Trump said it was too early to discuss guarantees before a Russia–Ukraine deal is reached.

squawks.headline: Iran dismisses reports that its oil tankers are being loaded as speculation
squawks.detail: Iran called reports about the loading of its oil tankers speculation, according to a market news feed. The statement comes while the US naval blockade of Iran remains in place.

squawks.headline: Germany's flash composite PMI rises to 55 from 53.4, with services at 54 and manufacturing at 55, all above forecasts
squawks.detail: Germany's November flash services PMI came in at 54, against a 52.3 forecast and 52.5 previously. Manufacturing rose to 55 from 54.2, above a 54.2 forecast, and the composite reached 55, above a 53.2 forecast.

squawks.headline: France's flash manufacturing PMI drops to 47.9 from 49.5 and the composite slips to 46.2, both below forecasts
squawks.detail: France's November flash manufacturing PMI came in at 47.9, against a 49.8 forecast and 49.5 previously. The flash composite PMI fell to 46.2 from 46.6, against a forecast of 47.9.

squawks.headline: France's flash services PMI rises to 46.6 from 46.2 but misses the 47.5 forecast
squawks.detail: France's November flash services PMI came in at 46.6, against a forecast of 47.5 and up from 46.2 the previous month.

squawks.headline: Ukraine sinks a Russian warship off Libya in a sea drone attack, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Ukraine sank a Russian warship off the Libyan coast. President Zelenskyy called the sea drone operation exemplary.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign ministry says Tehran will use every available means to counter the US naval blockade
squawks.detail: A spokesperson for Iran's foreign ministry said on Monday that Iran would use all the tools it has against the US naval blockade. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: First Secretary Haigh says the UK-EU deal will cut supermarket trading costs and backs state action where markets fail
squawks.detail: UK First Secretary of State Haigh said the government wants to intervene where markets are failing. She also said the UK-EU deal will lower trading costs for supermarkets.

squawks.headline: CBI warns public control talk deters investors as First Secretary Haigh moves to scrap some quangos
squawks.detail: The CBI business lobby group cautioned that government talk of public ownership puts investors off, the FT reports. Its warning comes as First Secretary Louise Haigh sets out plans to abolish some quangos.

squawks.headline: French finance minister Lescure warns the government's 1% GDP growth forecast for 2027 may be cut
squawks.detail: French Finance Minister Lescure said the government's 2027 economic growth forecast of 1% is at risk of being lowered.

squawks.headline: UK government to argue for more public sector control over utilities
squawks.detail: A market news account reports that the UK government will put forward the case for handing the public sector greater control of utilities. The report gave no further details.

squawks.headline: India's November HSBC composite PMI edges up to 56.3 from 56.2 as manufacturing rises and services slow
squawks.detail: The manufacturing PMI rose to 56 from 54.7, while the services PMI fell to 55.3 from 55.8.

squawks.headline: Asian regulators step up action to steady markets as AI-led selloff hits regional stocks
squawks.detail: The FT and WSJ report that regulators across Asia are increasing intervention to calm markets hit by the selloff in AI-related shares. Taiwan's stock exchange has asked listed companies to buy back shares and hold investor meetings.

squawks.headline: Sterling rises above $1.3100 after strong UK retail sales and as expectations of a hawkish Fed fade
squawks.detail: A market commentary feed reported that sterling moved past 1.3100 against the dollar in Asian trading on Monday. It linked the rise to upbeat UK retail sales figures and to fading expectations of hawkish Federal Reserve policy.

squawks.headline: Libya's NOC says pipeline valve closure will cut Sharara output by about 350,000 bpd
squawks.detail: Libya's National Oil Corporation said an unlawful group had closed a valve on the Sharara oil pipeline, causing a loss of around 350,000 barrels per day of production. Separately, Brent crude futures were reported down $1 at $91.57 a barrel in early trading.

squawks.headline: Trump says Iran fired more drones and missiles last week than at any time in over a year, all intercepted
squawks.detail: In a Truth Social post, the US president said Iran had launched more drones and missiles in the past week than at any point in more than a year, adding that all had been shot down without causing damage.

squawks.headline: European gas futures jump as much as 6.4% as trading opens for the week
squawks.detail: European natural gas prices rose as much as 6.4% at the start of Monday trading.

squawks.headline: Australia's flash composite PMI falls to 46.1 from 48.2
squawks.detail: Australia's flash services PMI fell to 46.2 from 48.5 and the flash manufacturing PMI fell to 48.7 from 49.6.

squawks.headline: Trump says he is inclined to resume strikes on Iran after the New Year if no deal is reached
squawks.detail: In an interview with Fox News, the US president dismissed Iran's talks and said he is leaning towards renewed strikes after the New Year if there is no deal. He also said any Iranian tankers that try to breach the US blockade would be sunk.

squawks.headline: Saudi civil defence issues an early warning alert over a possible threat in Riyadh
squawks.detail: Saudi Arabia's civil defence authority issued an early warning alert over a possible danger in the capital, Riyadh. It came after Houthi attacks on Saudi targets including Jazan and Al-Shuqaiq earlier in the day, and no further details were reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says more work is needed before the US can reach a fair trade deal with Canada
squawks.detail: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he is working on a fair trade deal with Canada but that more work remains before it can be agreed, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Iran's Araghchi wants Trump to say explicitly he seeks a deal and says the two-day Hormuz plan remains on offer
squawks.detail: Iran's foreign minister said Tehran needs confidence-building steps showing the US will not resume strikes. He said enriched uranium staying in Iran is a red line but he believes a fair solution is possible.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister Araghchi says Tehran sees no reason to replace the intermediaries in its peace talks with the US
squawks.detail: Iran's foreign minister Araghchi said Iran does not need to change the mediators used in the peace talks. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister Araghchi says Iran and the US are still exchanging messages through mediators
squawks.detail: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said messages between Tehran and Washington continue to pass through mediators. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister Araqchi says Tehran still hopes diplomacy can end its war with the US
squawks.detail: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi made the remarks in an interview with an Iranian newspaper. They come after he said earlier that the US blockade on Iran must be broken.

squawks.headline: EU is close to gaining a new trade power that would let it block access to its single market
squawks.detail: A market commentary account reports that the EU is nearing a new trade instrument allowing it to block access to the single market. No further details were given.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US is being patient on Iran
squawks.detail: US President Trump commented on Iran on Friday, after reports that he is weighing fresh strikes. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US military flags strain on its operations as Trump considers fresh strikes on Iran, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that US military officials have warned of operational pressure while President Trump weighs renewed attacks on Iran. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump threatens a heavy tax on data centres built outside the US, citing competition with China over AI
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the US president threatened a 'tremendous' tax on data centres built abroad, saying the aim is to stop Beijing taking the lead in AI development.

squawks.headline: US Treasury sanctions four Iranians accused of acting as oil trustees to collect overseas sale proceeds
squawks.detail: The US Treasury said it has imposed sanctions on four Iranian individuals who allegedly gathered proceeds from Iran's oil sales abroad to get around earlier sanctions.

squawks.headline: Trump weighs new strikes on Iran as hawkish US and Israeli officials push for action, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that President Trump is considering fresh strikes on Iran, with hawkish officials in Washington and Israel urging him to act. The same report says the US military has warned of strain on its forces.

squawks.headline: Bessent links his call for a smaller Fed hike to the energy supply shock and lower crude delivery prices
squawks.detail: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pointed to the energy supply shock and a fall in crude delivery prices as reasons the Federal Reserve should avoid a large rate hike, Reuters reports. He said some Fed governors are backing a big hike.

squawks.headline: Traders stop fully pricing a Fed rate hike in December
squawks.detail: A market newswire reports that traders no longer fully price a Fed rate rise at the December meeting. This comes on a day when US Treasury yields were reported falling.

squawks.headline: Fed's Paulson says investors seem to understand the Fed's communications
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve official Anna Paulson said investors appear to understand what the Fed is communicating. She spoke on Friday 20 November.

squawks.headline: Fed's Paulson says she is open to consecutive rate hikes and favours raising rates in a deliberate way
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve official Paulson said she would consider back-to-back rate increases and prefers a deliberate pace of tightening, according to posts on Friday evening.

squawks.headline: Trump says it is too early to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine before a Russia–Ukraine deal is reached
squawks.detail: US President Trump said on 20 November that security guarantees for Ukraine will not be discussed until there is a Ukraine–Russia deal, though the US will be involved.

squawks.headline: Global market selloff deepens this week as worries over AI and US interest rates drive selling across stocks, copper and gold
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that a global market rout got markedly worse this week. It says concerns about AI and US interest rates set off heavy selling across equities, copper and gold.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says inflation is clearly too high and raising France's retirement age would cut the deficit
squawks.detail: ECB policymaker Moulin said inflation is currently clearly too high. He also said that raising France's retirement age to match other European countries would lower the deficit.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US and China are exploring a wide-ranging deal, and wants only older-generation chips sold to China
squawks.detail: US President Trump said Washington and Beijing are discussing a comprehensive arrangement. He also said he wants restrictions that limit China to previous-generation semiconductors.

squawks.headline: Trump says the Iran war lifted oil far less than he expected, with oil near $80 rather than $300, and claims US control of Hormuz
squawks.detail: US President Trump said he had expected oil to reach $300 a barrel but it is now near $80, and that a record amount of oil had been taken out through the Strait of Hormuz, which he said the US controls.

squawks.headline: Rubio says Trump made progress on trade in talks with Canada's prime minister
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said the president met the Canadian prime minister to discuss trade and that progress was made.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says France faces a budget crisis but its banks and insurers are sound, and a deficit-cutting budget must pass
squawks.detail: ECB official Moulin said the French banking sector is not at risk and banks and insurers have solid foundations, while describing France as facing a budget crisis. He said approval of a budget that reduces the deficit is essential.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says France must address its high debt and deficit and curb spending growth
squawks.detail: ECB official Moulin said France needs measures to slow spending dynamics, while adding that its position is very different from Greece during its crisis.

squawks.headline: Fed's Cook says the Fed is watching how the AI build-out is financed and must tackle the inflation already present
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said the Fed is cautious about the funding behind the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure and will monitor the financial risks around it. She also said the Fed must deal with the inflation already in the economy, and that AI should support growth in the long run but will take time to raise productivity.

squawks.headline: Trump says he discussed Ukraine, Iran and reducing nuclear weapons risk with Xi and Putin at their China meeting
squawks.detail: US President Trump said the three leaders talked about Ukraine and Iran and about their responsibility to reduce the risks posed by nuclear weapons, and he described their three-way relationship as excellent. He also said Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.

squawks.headline: Fed's Cook says AI is displacing some jobs in parts of the US labour market
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Cook said she sees some job displacement caused by AI in parts of the labour market.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister says the US blockade on Iran must be broken, Iranian media report
squawks.detail: Iranian media reported the remarks by Iran's foreign minister on the US blockade. The posts gave no further details.

squawks.headline: Trump says Putin wants to end the Ukraine war through diplomacy and talks give a good chance of a deal
squawks.detail: US President Trump said Putin had told him he wanted the war in Ukraine to end by diplomatic means. Trump also said talks with Ukraine and Russia were going very well.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US is getting close to a trade deal with Mexico after talks with Sheinbaum
squawks.detail: US President Trump said on Friday that the US is nearing a trade deal with Mexico, following talks with Mexican President Sheinbaum. No terms or timing were given.

squawks.headline: US Treasury warns Singapore and Malaysia of risks if they fail to comply with US sanctions on Iran
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that US Treasury officials met government authorities in Singapore and Malaysia this week, including regulators and national security bodies, to warn of the risks of not complying with US sanctions on Iran.

squawks.headline: Trump says he and Xi agreed on joint measures for AI oversight
squawks.detail: US President Trump said he and Chinese President Xi reached agreement on joint oversight measures for artificial intelligence. In the same remarks he said US companies that build data centres outside the US would face a heavy tax.

squawks.headline: Trump says US interest rates are too high because of a politicised Fed and should be the lowest in the world
squawks.detail: The US President said the Federal Reserve is political, though he said he was not blaming its chairmen. In the same remarks he said he wants a real deal with Iran and that Tehran is interested in one, but not on terms he can accept.

squawks.headline: Trump says Iran will not offer a deal he can accept and US fuel prices depend on how the Iran dispute is settled
squawks.detail: At a press conference, US President Trump said crude oil prices have fallen 20% since the start of November, to close to $80 a barrel. He also said 10 more trade deals will be announced soon after his Asia trip.

squawks.headline: Sterling heads for a third weekly fall against the dollar as the dollar holds near its highest level since April 2025
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that sterling edged higher against the dollar on Friday but was on course for a third straight weekly loss. It says the dollar is being supported by expectations that the Federal Reserve will tighten policy and by concern about AI.

squawks.headline: Fed's Cook says September's hike fell short and recent data support further tightening, as high inflation leaves no room to wait
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said current policy is not restrictive enough to bring inflation down, financial conditions are too loose, and delaying hikes risks inflation becoming embedded, which would require a more aggressive response. She described US growth as strong and the labour market as stable, said the effect of tariffs on inflation is fading, and saw little sign yet of AI weighing on jobs.

squawks.headline: Houthis say they have attacked Saudi Arabia's Al-Shuqaiq power station and Jazan port
squawks.detail: The Houthis announced attacks on the Al-Shuqaiq power station and Jazan port in Saudi Arabia, after earlier threatening to strike the plant. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Citigroup's UK subsidiary underreported $35bn of assets, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that Citigroup's UK subsidiary underreported its assets by $35bn. The report gives no market reaction.

squawks.headline: China's $2bn dollar bond draws over $72bn of orders and prices in line with US Treasuries
squawks.detail: A bookrunner's message seen by Reuters shows China's $2bn bond drew more than $72bn in orders. It priced in line with US Treasuries, not at the 25bp premium first suggested.

squawks.headline: Russia is considering restarting jet fuel exports, Tass reports
squawks.detail: Russian state news agency Tass reports that Russia is weighing a resumption of jet fuel exports. No timing or volumes were given.

squawks.headline: Iranian official says Qeshm Island blast came from disposal of unexploded munitions, after earlier missile attack report
squawks.detail: Tasnim, which had earlier reported a missile strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, quoted an official who said the explosion and smoke came from the disposal of unexploded munitions.

squawks.headline: Eurogroup names Germany's Brunnermeier and France's Laurence Boone as candidates for ECB chief economist
squawks.detail: The Eurogroup named German economist Markus Brunnermeier and French economist and banker Laurence Boone as candidates for the post of ECB chief economist.

squawks.headline: Trump administration tells European and Ukrainian officials it wants a Ukraine–Russia peace deal by early January, reports say
squawks.detail: Reports, including the FT, say the Trump administration has told European and Ukrainian officials it wants Kyiv to reach a peace deal with Russia before January. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

squawks.headline: Missile strikes Iran's Qeshm Island in the south, Tasnim reports, with no details yet on damage
squawks.detail: Iran's Tasnim News Agency reported a missile hit Qeshm Island in southern Iran and gave no information on any damage. The report did not say who fired the missile.

squawks.headline: European gas futures climb as much as 5% to €88.7/MWh
squawks.detail: European gas futures were reported up by as much as 5% on the day, reaching €88.7/MWh.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield extends its fall to 10bp on the day, at 4.95%
squawks.detail: A market wire reports the US 10-year Treasury yield down 10bp on the day at 4.95%. Earlier it was reported 8bp lower at 4.9698%.

squawks.headline: Bessent says Iran's threats show US sanctions are putting it under pressure
squawks.detail: US Treasury Secretary Bessent said Iran's threats suggest US sanctions are squeezing the country. He made the remarks while also commenting on the Fed.

squawks.headline: Bessent says Hormuz crude flows overnight were the largest since the conflict began and the US will keep pressuring Iran's IRGC
squawks.detail: In a CNBC interview, US Treasury Secretary Bessent said the US will keep squeezing the IRGC until it is ready for a deal, and that Russia and China agree Iran cannot have nuclear weapons. He said the most crude oil since the conflict started passed through the Strait of Hormuz overnight.

squawks.headline: US Treasury Secretary Bessent questions the case for a bigger Fed hike and says the Fed should focus on the outlook
squawks.detail: In a CNBC interview, US Treasury Secretary Bessent said it seemed erratic for the Fed to want a larger rate hike. He said the Fed should look ahead rather than at past data.

squawks.headline: US 5-year Treasury yield drops 10bp on the day to 4.75%
squawks.detail: The US 5-year Treasury yield is reported 10bp lower on the day at 4.75%. Earlier, the 10-year yield was reported down 8bp.

squawks.headline: Bessent says the H200 remains the US chip threshold for China and the US will ensure restrictions hold and remote access is curtailed
squawks.detail: US Treasury Secretary Bessent said the Nvidia H200 is still the limit for chip sales to China, that China has placed few orders for it, and that remote access to restricted chips has been curtailed. He also said Presidents Xi and Trump will meet for a fourth time at the G20 in Florida.

squawks.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts two Houthi ballistic missiles fired at Jazan, with debris landing in the Al-Shuqaiq area
squawks.detail: The coalition said its air defences destroyed two ballistic missiles launched towards the Jazan region and that authorities are going to the site where debris fell. The Houthis had earlier threatened to target Saudi Arabia's Shuqaiq power plant.

squawks.headline: US Treasury Secretary Bessent says Trump's China trip included in-depth talks on trade policy and AI
squawks.detail: Speaking to CNBC, Bessent said Trump and Xi agreed that humans should stay involved in any military decisions made by AI. He also said AI-based attacks come from Chinese models.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says OBR forecasts make the 2020s the worst decade on record for income growth
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation, citing the latest OBR forecasts, says incomes are set to end 2030 just 1.4% higher than in 2020.

squawks.headline: EU commits a further €1bn through the European Peace Facility for Ukraine's armed forces
squawks.detail: The EU says the money will go on joint procurement of lethal and non-lethal equipment for Ukraine's armed forces.

squawks.headline: Eurozone flash consumer confidence rises to -16.9, beating the -18 forecast
squawks.detail: The flash eurozone consumer confidence reading was -16.9, compared with a -18 forecast and -17.9 previously.

squawks.headline: University of Michigan final sentiment comes in at 51.5, and 1-year inflation expectations ease to 3.7% from 4.3%
squawks.detail: In the final University of Michigan survey, sentiment was 51.5 against a 51.6 forecast and 51.0 previously. Expectations rose to 52.9 against a 51.2 forecast, and current conditions fell to 49.4 against a 52.3 forecast. 1-year inflation expectations were 3.7% against a 4.2% forecast, and 5-year expectations were 3.3% against a 3.4% forecast and 3.4% previously.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham and EU's von der Leyen and Costa condemn Russian violation of Polish airspace
squawks.detail: UK Prime Minister Burnham said the incursion into Poland was unacceptable. European Commission President von der Leyen condemned the violation and expressed solidarity with Poland, and EU Council President Costa said Russia was going in the wrong direction.

squawks.headline: USTR Greer says any US–China truce extension depends on rare earths and Section 301 investigations are due before year-end
squawks.detail: US Trade Representative Greer said Chinese agricultural purchases and rare earths would build goodwill, and that China raised Taiwan in this week's talks. He said Section 301 investigations will come before the end of the year.

squawks.headline: Burnham says the UK–EU reset deal is done and tuition fees will be discussed further; von der Leyen expects a solution
squawks.detail: UK Prime Minister Burnham said there was no confusion over tuition fees and that further talks would follow on issues including fees. European Commission President von der Leyen said she was confident of a solution with the UK on tuition fees and welcomed Burnham's willingness to have an EU debate.

squawks.headline: Saudi-led coalition strikes Hodeidah port and says its operation continues in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz
squawks.detail: The Saudi-led coalition said it hit capabilities at Yemen's Hodeidah port that it said were used for smuggling and moving weapons and ballistic missiles. It said the operation to destroy targets in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz is still under way.

squawks.headline: Burnham says the EU deal is probably as far as the UK can go before 2029 and proposes informal talks with the EU in about a year
squawks.detail: Speaking alongside von der Leyen and Costa, UK Prime Minister Burnham said the UK needs to consider its right long-term relationship with the EU and linked it to his 10-year plan. He proposed informal brainstorming with the EU on options for the next parliament, and von der Leyen said the EU is open to this.

squawks.headline: Saudi-led coalition launches an operation against Houthi threat sources in Yemen
squawks.detail: The Saudi-led coalition said it has begun an operation to neutralise sources of threats used to target civilians in Yemen and Saudi Arabia, including vital sources supporting the Houthis' military efforts. This follows Houthi threats against Saudi infrastructure.

squawks.headline: Canadian core retail sales rise 1.0% on the month, above the 0.7% forecast
squawks.detail: Canadian core retail sales rose 1.0% month on month in September, against a 0.7% forecast and 1.2% previously.

squawks.headline: Canadian retail sales rise 0.8% on the month, above the 0.7% forecast
squawks.detail: Canadian retail sales grew 0.8% month on month, against a 0.7% forecast and down from 1.2% previously.

squawks.headline: Burnham says the Treasury puts the UK–EU deal's boost at up to 0.5% of GDP, or £17bn, with a bill due next week
squawks.detail: Speaking after the Brussels summit, Burnham said the Treasury estimates the reset deal will add up to 0.5% of UK GDP, a £17bn boost to the economy. He said legislation to implement the deal will be brought forward next week.

squawks.headline: ECB's Nagel says the ECB needs to act at its December meeting
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Nagel said he believes the ECB has to do something at the December meeting. He added that this would put policy in slightly restrictive territory.

squawks.headline: UK officials say the EU reset deal could lead the UK to mirror EU tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports the comments from UK officials after the UK–EU summit. Earlier, Business Secretary Reynolds said UK tariff decisions would serve UK industry and would not simply follow the EU's lead.

squawks.headline: ECB's Nagel says inflation is too high and policy is slightly restrictive, with inflation expectations well anchored
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Nagel also said German GDP should grow 1.3% this year and about the same in 2027. In an earlier remark in the same appearance he put this year's growth at around 1.2%.

squawks.headline: Europe's STOXX 600 is down 5.58% this week, on track for its biggest weekly fall since March–April 2025
squawks.detail: A market wire reports that the pan-European STOXX 600 index has lost 5.58% so far this week.

squawks.headline: Von der Leyen says the UK will join Erasmus+ from next year, and work on UK participation in the EU electricity market continues
squawks.detail: At the UK–EU summit, European Commission President von der Leyen said the UK will take part in Erasmus+ from next year and that work on UK participation in the electricity market is still going on. She also announced a dialogue on economic security and a digital partnership, and confirmed that talks on youth experience, agri-food trade and linking carbon markets have concluded.

squawks.headline: EU Council President Costa says talks are concluded on a framework for UK participation in EU civil missions
squawks.detail: Speaking at the UK–EU summit, Costa said the EU respects the UK's 2016 decision to leave and any choice the UK makes on the long-term relationship. He added that the EU remains open to the closest possible relationship with the UK.

squawks.headline: UK–EU summit statement links emissions trading systems from 2028 and eases agri-food trade from March 2028
squawks.detail: The joint statement from the Brussels summit also sets out a youth mobility scheme for 100,000 people from each side, to be available by January 2030, and a plan to agree lower university tuition fees within six months. Both sides also agreed to set up a dialogue on economic security and to limit harm to each other's supply chains.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield falls 8bp to 4.9698%
squawks.detail: A market news feed reported the 10-year US Treasury note yield down 8bp at 4.9698% shortly before 13:00 GMT.

squawks.headline: Ukrainian drone strikes cut Russian refinery crude processing by 45% since late October, and more regions limit fuel sales
squawks.detail: Reuters reported, citing industry sources, that Ukrainian drone attacks have cut Russian refineries' combined crude processing by 45% since late October. More Russian regions are now limiting fuel sales.

squawks.headline: US and Israel are weighing a fresh assault on Iran in the near term, CBS reports, citing sources
squawks.detail: CBS reported, citing unnamed sources, that the US and Israel are considering a new attack on Iran in the short term. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

squawks.headline: European Commission President von der Leyen calls the UK–EU reset deal a turning point in relations
squawks.detail: Von der Leyen welcomed the agreement reached at Friday's UK–EU summit, describing it as a turning point for EU–UK relations.

squawks.headline: Houthis name a Saudi financial centre in King Abdullah Economic City as a military target and tell people to stay away
squawks.detail: The Houthis said the financial centre in King Abdullah Economic City, which they placed in Riyadh, is now a target for their forces and urged staff and citizens to leave the area immediately. The statement follows their earlier threats against Saudi power plants, ports and airspace.

squawks.headline: Burnham calls the UK–EU reset deal a landmark agreement and a good day for Britain and Europe
squawks.detail: The Prime Minister spoke on the agreement reached at Friday's UK–EU summit. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: France seeks a UN Security Council meeting after Russian strikes on Kyiv that hit the Austrian and Dutch embassies
squawks.detail: France's foreign minister called for the Security Council meeting after the latest Russian strikes on Kyiv, which included hits on the Austrian and Dutch embassies.

squawks.headline: Houthis say they will target Saudi Arabia's Shuqaiq power plant within hours in retaliation for strikes on Yemeni power stations
squawks.detail: In a statement, Yemen's Houthis said the attack on Saudi Arabia's Shuqaiq power plant was retaliation for strikes on the Saada and Mocha power stations. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Poland's Tusk asks NATO for an immediate boost to air defences after Russian missiles land on Polish territory
squawks.detail: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk called for NATO to strengthen Poland's air defences without delay. The request follows the day's incident in which Poland said Russian missiles and a drone came down on its territory.

squawks.headline: Poland's Tusk says the day's airspace incident shows Poland must take part in Ukraine peace talks
squawks.detail: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incident involving Russian missiles landing on Polish territory showed why Poland needs a place in the Ukraine peace talks.

squawks.headline: Russia's foreign ministry says Moscow will respond with diplomatic countermeasures to Estonia's border closure
squawks.detail: Russia's foreign ministry said Moscow will take diplomatic countermeasures after Estonia announced it will close its border crossings with Russia. The ministry did not give details of the measures.

squawks.headline: Houthis warn airlines that Saudi airspace is unsafe ahead of planned operations in the coming hours
squawks.detail: The Yemen-based Houthi movement told all aviation companies that airspace over Saudi Arabia would be the scene of its operations in the coming hours, excluding the airspace over Mecca and Medina. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

squawks.headline: EU pays out €7.9bn to Ukraine
squawks.detail: The European Union has disbursed €7.9bn to Ukraine, according to a market news feed. No further details were given.

squawks.headline: Poland's Tusk calls the Russian missiles that fell on Polish territory a deliberate provocation and an escalation
squawks.detail: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Poland is certain the objects that came down on its territory were Russian, that the incident does not look accidental, and that it is the latest example of Russian escalation. He said he had spoken with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte.

squawks.headline: Russia says EU foreign policy chief Kallas is unsuitable to negotiate with Moscow and her role could collapse talks
squawks.detail: Russia said EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas would be a wholly unsuitable negotiator with Moscow. It added that her involvement in the talks could lead to their breakdown. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Houthis threaten Saudi Red Sea ports if Hodeidah is bombed and call for evacuations
squawks.detail: A Houthi spokesman warned that Saudi ports on the Red Sea would be targeted if the Saudi-led coalition bombs Hodeidah, and called for evacuations. The coalition had earlier told civilians to leave Hodeidah port after Houthi attacks on Riyadh.

squawks.headline: Burnham agrees UK–EU deal to begin reversing parts of Brexit, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Prime Minister Andy Burnham has agreed the long-awaited UK–EU reset deal. No further terms were given in the report.

squawks.headline: US limits on China's access to advanced AI chips weigh further on Chinese tech stocks this week
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that several US measures restricting China's access to advanced AI chips pushed Chinese technology shares lower this week. Investors are weighing whether the curbs will slow Beijing's plans or speed up its push to make its own chips.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Russia fired more than 110 missiles and 400 drones at Ukraine in one of its largest attacks
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy gave the figures for the latest Russian attack and called it one of the most massive of the war. Earlier reports said the strikes hit Kyiv's bridges and energy infrastructure, and Kyiv brought in emergency blackouts.

squawks.headline: Saudi-led coalition tells civilians to leave Yemen's Hodeidah port after Houthi attacks on Riyadh
squawks.detail: The coalition's Joint Forces Command published a call for civilians to evacuate the Red Sea port of Hodeidah, citing their safety. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: EU says terms of UK reset deal depend on UK charging EU students the same tuition fees as British students
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Andy Burnham is set to agree the deal, while the EU says its terms depend on the UK giving European students the same tuition fees as UK students.

squawks.headline: Hungary reportedly lifts its veto, letting Ukraine open the last two EU accession clusters
squawks.detail: Market reports say Hungary has withdrawn its veto, allowing Ukraine to open the final two clusters of its EU accession negotiations. No official confirmation was included in the reports.

squawks.headline: Traders scale back ECB rate-hike bets and now price only two hikes by the end of 2027
squawks.detail: Money market traders have reduced their bets on ECB tightening. Pricing now points to two rate hikes by the end of 2027.

squawks.headline: No.10 says UK–EU summit negotiations have concluded and the deal is done, with talks continuing in some areas
squawks.detail: Downing Street said the UK–EU summit deal has been agreed and both sides have settled when it will come into force, with the dates set out in a joint statement. Talks will continue on some areas.

squawks.headline: Estonia to shut its border crossings with Russia from 1 December and will review the closure after 6 months
squawks.detail: The Estonian government says its border crossings with Russia will close from 1 December onwards and that it will reconsider the decision in 6 months.

squawks.headline: Polish general says 11 objects threatened Polish airspace and 3 of them crossed into it
squawks.detail: General Nowak of Poland's military gave the figures on Friday as the incursion story continued, after Poland said missiles and a drone that came down on its territory came from Russia.

squawks.headline: Poland says two missiles and a drone that came down on its territory came from Russia and will ask NATO for more support
squawks.detail: Poland's defence minister said a Russian KH-101 cruise missile likely fell in Poland, called it another Russian provocation and linked its timing to a meeting of the coalition of the willing. He said Poland will ask NATO for additional support.

squawks.headline: ECB's Santos Pereira says the ECB will keep acting decisively on rates as inflation risks increase
squawks.detail: ECB policymaker Santos Pereira said inflationary pressure is significant, risks are rising and the ECB will continue to act decisively on interest rates.

squawks.headline: UK Business Secretary says the aim of the EU reset is now to stop new trade barriers from emerging
squawks.detail: The Business Secretary described the goal of the Burnham-led UK–EU reset as preventing new barriers to trade. A UK politics journalist noted that this differs from the broader options set out at party conference.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says Russia will not win the war and links Ukraine aid and investment to reforms
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz said he had told Ukraine that fast-moving reforms are the basis for investment and financial aid. He also said Russian hybrid attacks on Germany are increasing every month.

squawks.headline: ECB's Santos Pereira says energy-driven inflation pressures are still significant
squawks.detail: ECB policymaker Santos Pereira said energy is still driving significant inflation pressures. He said the key question is whether energy price pressures spread to the rest of the economy.

squawks.headline: Saudi Arabia starts refilling joint crude storage in Japan, and Japan plans to buy 8m barrels of Saudi oil for its own reserve
squawks.detail: Saudi state news agency SPA says Japan will offer 16m barrels of oil storage and Saudi Arabia has begun refilling the joint crude storage in Japan. Separately, Japan plans to buy 8m barrels of Saudi crude for its own reserve, and both countries stressed the importance of a stable oil market.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lagarde names AI combined with cyber threats as the challenge that worries her most
squawks.detail: ECB President Lagarde said the combination of artificial intelligence and cyber threats is the challenge that concerns her most. She made no reference to rates in the reported remarks.

squawks.headline: EU and UK agree a youth mobility scheme for 100,000 young people from each side, EU official says
squawks.detail: An EU official says the EU and the UK have agreed a youth mobility scheme for 100,000 young people from both sides. The agreement comes on the day of the UK–EU reset summit.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lagarde says the ECB's swap lines will become easier to access
squawks.detail: ECB President Christine Lagarde said the central bank's swap lines will be made more accessible. No further details were given in the report.

squawks.headline: European bond sales go above €2 trillion for the first time
squawks.detail: Bond issuance in Europe has passed €2 trillion for the first time, according to a market newswire report.

squawks.headline: Ukraine's nuclear plants reduce output after Russian strikes on energy grid, with outages in Kyiv and ten regions
squawks.detail: Ukraine's deputy energy minister says the nuclear power plants cut output after Russian attacks on energy distribution. He says the overnight strikes caused power cuts in Kyiv and ten regions.

squawks.headline: Burnham is set to sign the UK–EU reset deal in Brussels, covering freer food and drink trade and a youth scheme
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Burnham will sign the UK–EU reset agreement in Brussels. The deal provides for closer ties, including freer trade in food and drink and a youth experience scheme.

squawks.headline: French Budget Minister Amiel says an extra €6bn budget effort is only a starting point for 2027
squawks.detail: France's Budget Minister Amiel described the additional €6bn of budget effort as a starting point for 2027 fiscal plans. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: French overall business climate slips to 95 in November, below the 96 forecast, while the manufacturing index reaches 104
squawks.detail: France's overall business climate index fell to 95 from 97, compared with a forecast of 96. The manufacturing index was 104, down from 105 but above the 103 forecast.

squawks.headline: ONS revises UK April–September borrowing down by £3.6bn, citing stronger tax receipts
squawks.detail: With the October public finances release, the ONS lowered its estimate of the 2026/27 deficit for April to September by £3.6bn. It put the revision down to stronger tax receipts data.

squawks.headline: UK and EU expected to agree easier food trade and youth mobility at Friday's reset summit, with divisions still in place
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Britain and the European Union are expected to agree to ease food trade and youth mobility at a summit on Friday as part of a reset of ties. The report adds that the summit is also likely to show disagreements that remain over the longer-term relationship.

squawks.headline: ONS says UK supermarkets reported stronger October sales after government advice to buy long-life items
squawks.detail: The ONS gave the supermarket comment alongside the October retail sales release.

squawks.headline: German producer prices rise 8.1% year on year in October, above the 7.3% forecast
squawks.detail: German PPI rose 1.4% on the month against a 1% forecast and 1.9% previously; the annual rate rose from 6.7% in September.

squawks.headline: Swedish seasonally adjusted unemployment falls to 8.2% in October, below forecasts
squawks.detail: The seasonally adjusted rate fell from 8.6%, against forecasts of 8.55% to 8.6%; the unadjusted rate was 7.7% against 8.1% previously.

squawks.headline: UK public sector net borrowing comes in at £17.0bn in October, below the £18bn estimate and down from £24.5bn
squawks.detail: ONS data show October PSNB ex banking groups at £17.036bn against an estimate of £18bn and £24.52bn the previous month. The public sector net cash requirement was £10.8bn and the central government net cash requirement £15.5bn, both against £16.9bn previously.

squawks.headline: UK retail sales rise 0.7% on the month against a flat forecast, and core sales gain 0.9%
squawks.detail: Headline UK retail sales rose 0.7% month on month, against a 0% forecast and -0.4% previously, and were up 2.3% year on year, against 1.7% forecast and 0.8% previously. Core sales rose 0.9% on the month, against 0.1% forecast and -0.7% previously, and 2.5% on the year, against 1.8% forecast and 0.8% previously.

squawks.headline: Russia's foreign ministry says there is no agreement yet on the next round of Ukraine talks
squawks.detail: Russia's foreign ministry said no date has been agreed for further Ukraine negotiations, according to Interfax. Separately, the ministry said Moscow is preparing to host European Union representatives.

squawks.headline: Sri Lanka's central bank governor says rate cuts will resume after inflation moves lower
squawks.detail: Sri Lanka's central bank governor said the bank will go back to cutting rates now that inflation has fallen. No timing or size of cuts was given in the report.

squawks.headline: South Korea's KOSPI closes down 5.21% at its weakest level since 16 January
squawks.detail: South Korea's KOSPI index ended Friday's session 5.21% lower, its weakest close since 16 January, as the sell-off across Asian markets continued.

squawks.headline: Gold heads for its worst week in eight months as a firm dollar and bets on a December Fed hike weigh
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that gold slipped on Friday and was on course for its worst week in eight months. It says a resilient US dollar and expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December weighed on prices.

squawks.headline: UK Business Secretary Reynolds says UK tariff decisions will serve UK industry, not simply follow the EU's lead
squawks.detail: Business Secretary Reynolds said the UK would set tariff policy in the interest of its own industry rather than copying EU measures, and that both sides stand to gain a lot from EU-UK trade. He also said financial services were neglected in the original Brexit negotiations.

squawks.headline: Oil rises on supply worries after Houthi attacks on Riyadh and reported tanker disruption in Hormuz
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that oil prices rose on Friday after Houthi attacks on the Saudi capital and reports of tanker disruption in the Strait of Hormuz. Prices were still on course for a weekly fall.

squawks.headline: BoJ policymakers mostly agree a rate hike is needed next month but differ on how far rates should rise, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Bank of Japan policymakers broadly back a rate rise next month. They are split on where rates should eventually peak.

squawks.headline: Russia carries out its biggest strikes on Kyiv's bridges of the war and hits energy infrastructure, and Kyiv brings in emergency blackouts
squawks.detail: Kyiv's mayor said a Russian ballistic missile attack hit three bridges over the Dnipro and killed three people. Russia's defence ministry said it had targeted energy and transport infrastructure, and city officials introduced emergency blackouts.
